summary.en-US: Live captions transcribed from a video's actual audio, word for word. For language learning. DRM-protected sites need the free companion app.
summary.es-ES: Subtítulos en vivo transcritos del audio real del video, palabra por palabra. Para aprender idiomas. Los sitios con DRM necesitan la app companion gratuita.

description.en-US:
Captions transcribes what is actually said in a video, live, and shows it on top of the player. Unlike platform subtitles, which are often translated separately from a dub, the text matches the audio word for word, which makes it useful for learning a language by watching series and films. How it works
  • Pick the audio language and a speech-to-text provider in the settings.
  • On a page with a video, click the toolbar button → Start captions, or press Alt+Shift+C.
  • Captions follow the video: pausing, seeking and playback speed stay in sync, and rewinding replays lines already transcribed.
Providers
  • Deepgram (cloud): fast (about 0.6 s behind the audio) and accurate. Needs your own Deepgram API key (they give free credit on signup).
  • Local server: Whisper on your own computer through WhisperLiveKit. Free and private, but slower.
  • Test signal: shows the audio level, to check capture on a site without spending credit.
DRM-protected videos (Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video…) Firefox doesn't let extensions read the audio of DRM-protected videos. For those, install the free Captions companion app once, outside the browser (Windows 10/11, or Linux with PipeWire). It records only Firefox's sound output, only while captions are on. The settings page tells you whether it's installed and links to the download: https://github.com/Josueccc/captions/releases/latest Everything else works without it. Privacy The extension has no server of its own and no analytics. Video audio goes only to the provider you configure, only while captions are on. Source code: https://github.com/Josueccc/captions
description.es-ES:
Captions transcribe en vivo lo que realmente se dice en un video y lo muestra sobre el reproductor. A diferencia de los subtítulos de la plataforma, que a menudo se traducen aparte del doblaje, el texto coincide palabra por palabra con el audio, lo que lo hace útil para aprender idiomas viendo series y películas. Cómo funciona
  • Elige el idioma del audio y un proveedor de transcripción en los ajustes.
  • En una página con video, pulsa el botón de la barra → Iniciar subtítulos, o Alt+Shift+C.
  • Los subtítulos siguen al video: pausar, saltar y cambiar la velocidad se mantienen sincronizados, y al retroceder se repiten las líneas ya transcritas.
Proveedores
  • Deepgram (nube): rápido (unos 0,6 s de retraso) y preciso. Necesita tu propia clave de API de Deepgram (dan crédito gratis al registrarse).
  • Servidor local: Whisper en tu propio equipo mediante WhisperLiveKit. Gratis y privado, pero más lento.
  • Señal de prueba: muestra el nivel de audio, para comprobar la captura en un sitio sin gastar crédito.
Videos con DRM (Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video…) Firefox no deja que las extensiones lean el audio de los videos con DRM. Para esos, instala una vez la aplicación gratuita Captions companion, fuera del navegador (Windows 10/11, o Linux con PipeWire). Solo graba la salida de sonido de Firefox, y solo mientras los subtítulos están activos. La página de ajustes te dice si está instalada y enlaza a la descarga: https://github.com/Josueccc/captions/releases/latest Todo lo demás funciona sin ella. Privacidad La extensión no tiene servidor propio ni analíticas. El audio del video solo va al proveedor que configures, y solo mientras los subtítulos están activos. Código fuente: https://github.com/Josueccc/captions

version.approval_notes:
Build from the attached source archive (identical to the GitHub tag):
  Node 22, then: npm ci && npm run build
  Output: dist/ (bundled with esbuild, not minified; source maps included).

Testing without an account: Settings → Transcription provider → "Test signal". Open any page with a non-DRM <video> (e.g. a YouTube video), click the toolbar button → Start captions. It shows the audio level instead of text. The Deepgram provider needs an API key (free credit at deepgram.com).

Permissions:
- <all_urls> host permission + content script: finds the <video> on any site, reads its audio with mozCaptureStream() while captions are on, and draws the caption overlay. Nothing runs until the user starts captions.
- nativeMessaging: optional companion app (source in companion/, Rust; releases on GitHub) used only for DRM-protected videos, whose audio Firefox won't expose to extensions. It records Firefox's sound output after decoding, like OS live captions do; it doesn't touch the video or its decryption. The extension works without it; the settings page only checks whether it's installed ("hello" message, nothing recorded).
- storage: settings and the user's own API key, kept in storage.local.

Data: audio goes only to the provider the user configures (Deepgram with their own key, or a server they run, localhost by default). No analytics. Privacy policy: PRIVACY.md in the repo.
